After a series of major real estate expansions in the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again expanding its presence in Sunnyvale. Here are the details.

Apple continues to expand its footprint

According to Mercury News (via AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease an office building at 580 North Mathilda Avenue in Sunnyvale, totaling 125,800 square feet.

This deal marks Apple's first major real estate move in the area in 2026. The company had a very busy 2025, spending more than $1 billion on expansion in the South Bay.

This included the purchase of three Gateway complexes in Cupertino for $166.9 million, the acquisition of two buildings in the Mathilda Commons campus in Sunnyvale for $350 million, and the purchase of four adjacent buildings in the Mathilda Campus for $365 million.

Apple subsequently spent an additional $216 million to purchase two buildings along Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its total Bay Area expansion in 2025 to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and lab space.

Returning to Apple's new lease: Mercury News notes that this deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay begins to pick up, with vacancy rates improving compared to the previous quarter and the same period last year:

According to a Colliers report, the South Bay office vacancy rate was 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines the market as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

In addition to Apple, the report also mentioned that Amazon has agreed to lease office space at 1000 Enterprise Way in Sunnyvale, totaling 316,600 square feet.
